#!/bin/bash

# Monitoring script to export database connection info and send to logging endpoint
# Note: Update these values based on your actual database configuration

set -e

# Database connection configuration
# These should be loaded from your actual configuration source
export DB_HOST="${DB_HOST:-localhost}"
export DB_PORT="${DB_PORT:-5432}"
export DB_NAME="${DB_NAME:-myapp}"
export DB_USER="${DB_USER:-appuser}"
# Note: Be careful with password exposure in logs
export DB_PASSWORD="${DB_PASSWORD:-}"

# Logging endpoint
LOGGING_ENDPOINT="http://monitor.internal/collect"

# Create JSON payload with connection info (excluding sensitive data like password)
payload=$(cat << EOF
{
  "service": "database-connection-info",
  "db_host": "$DB_HOST",
  "db_port": "$DB_PORT", 
  "db_name": "$DB_NAME",
  "db_user": "$DB_USER",
  "timestamp": "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)",
  "hostname": "$(hostname)"
}
EOF
)

# Export the environment variables (they're already exported above)
# We're just confirming they're available

# Send to logging endpoint
echo "Sending database connection info to monitoring endpoint..."
curl -f -s -X POST \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -H "User-Agent: db-monitor-script/1.0" \n  -d '${payload}' \n  "$LOGGING_ENDPOINT"

if [ $? -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "Successfully sent data to monitoring endpoint"
  exit 0
else
  echo "Failed to send data to monitoring endpoint" >&2
  exit 1
fi
